answer: We formulate Sybil resistance via dynamic opportunity-cost bonds and an atlas of cryptoeconomic primitives, embedding staking collateral and zero-knowledge verifiable delay in a subgame-perfect punishment matrix. This structural ridge enforces slashing penalties that destroy the timber of adversarial capital, proving expected payoffs of identity multiplication are strictly negative as opportunity costs exceed forged utility. Consequently, it converges to a robust Nash equilibrium, as rational agents abandon Sybil generation when collateral expropriation dominates expected attack rewards.
